title: Initiative Contracts and Release‑Gating Playbook for Company OKRs
creator: Avery Chen
description:
Summary:
This ticket captures a pragmatic, cross-functional playbook for converting company-level OKRs into scoped initiative "contracts" and defining deterministic release gates. The intent is to reduce ambiguity between product, engineering, design, and go-to-market when committing to initiatives that influence company OKRs.

Goals:
- Create a lightweight "initiative contract" template teams sign to confirm scope, acceptance criteria, key metrics, and rollback conditions.
- Define a clear set of release gates (e.g., metrics, infra readiness, docs & runbook, compliance) that must be satisfied before an initiative marks as "done" against OKRs.
- Provide a standard signoff flow and timing so canary/cutover decisions are predictable across hundreds of initiatives.
- Integrate gating signals into Console dashboards and Linear so program managers and execs can see gating state in one place.

What an "Initiative Contract" contains (template):
- Initiative name and owner(s)
- OKR mapping: objective id(s) and target delta (quantitative where possible)
- Commitment level: Committed | Target | Stretch (teams pick one)
- Primary success metrics (1–3) and measurement queries/dashboards
- Non-functional constraints: latency SLO, cost uplift budget, availability target
- Release gates required: list from gating matrix (see below)
- Rollback criteria and automated rollback/kill-switch plan
- Cross-functional signoffs: PM, ENG lead, Design, SEC/Compliance, Sales/CS (if customer-facing)
- Delivery checklist and owner for each artifact (PR, migration plan, console dashboard, release notes)

Release gating matrix (example gates):
- Metric validation: metric-sidecar dashboard green for at least 72 hours in staging — required for all customer-impacting initiatives
- Performance SLO: tail latency measured and under agreed limit on canary traffic
- Error budget: initiative must not cause error budget burn > 15% in staging or pre-prod
- Safety/Compliance: required for initiatives touching PII or VPC customers (SEC signoff)
- Operational readiness: runbook, pager rotations, on-call playbook, and rollback steps present
- Documentation: end-user docs + internal runbook + marketing-facing one-pager

Signoff flow and timing (practical guidance):
- During planning (Cycle kickoff): PM creates Initiative Contract draft and attaches to Linear ticket. Engineering and Design fill technical constraints and acceptance criteria.
- Two-week before planned release: PM triggers a gated review checklist in Linear; owners must mark gates as "ready" or provide mitigation plans.
- Eight business days before release: stakeholders must either sign off or raise a formal Blocker. Blockers default to "Escalate to Initiative Sponsor" cadence.
- Canary window: monitor gating dashboards. If any gate trips (performance, errors, or security), the on-call owner executes rollback plan.

Measuring success and OKR alignment:
- For each initiative contract we require a baseline and a post-release measurement query; PMs must link dashboards and provide expected delta (absolute and relative).
- We will quarterly audit 10% of initiative contracts against claimed OKR impact to validate calibration of commitment levels.

Integrations and tooling recommendations:
- Linear: add "Initiative Contract" attachment type and a gating checklist section; expose gating state as a custom field on tickets.
- Console: add a gating dashboard widget that aggregates gating states for initiatives mapped to a company OKR.
- GitHub: require PR template to reference Initiative Contract ID.
- PagerDuty: link runbook & on-call rotation in contract metadata.

Edge cases and trade-offs:
- We will not require exhaustive formal signoffs for trivial infra tasks; apply a triage rule based on customer impact and risk tier.
- Commitments for exploratory research work default to "Target" or "Stretch" to avoid over-committing.
- Heavy-handed gating increases ceremony; playbook aims to be minimal but auditable.

Next steps (actionable):
1) Iterate contract template with Eng/Design/Sec and lock the first iteration by 2026-02-24.
2) Build Linear custom field and checklist prototype (ENG-3472) and ship soft rollout to 3 pilot teams.
3) Add gating widget to Console (PM-22110) and wire sample dashboards for pilot initiatives.
4) Run pilot across 5 initiatives in 2026-Q1 and evaluate friction/accuracy.

Deliverables:
- Initiative contract template (Google Doc link in attachments)
- Linear checklist/template and example tickets for 5 pilots
- Console gating dashboard prototype
- Post-pilot retrospective with calibration recommendations
